title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwriting is written over a typed Bourbaki page (Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats, n° 382). The mathematics is the Hodge–Tate analysis of a Lubin–Tate (CM-type, height h, dimension 1) ℓ-adic Galois representation.

Setup (reconstructed):
- A is a finite extension of Q_ℓ, contained in the local field K.
- π = Gal(K̄/K), and C is the completion of K̄.
- V_ℓ is the rational Tate module of a 1-dimensional formal group with formal multiplication by O_A, so V_ℓ is free of rank 1 over A.
- π acts on V_ℓ through a character χ_π : π → A*, the Lubin–Tate character.
- A⊗_{Q_ℓ}C ≅ ∏_σ C_σ, the product running over the embeddings σ : A → C.

The canonical isomorphisms 'obtained above' are V_ℓ⊗_A C ≅ C_1 and V_ℓ^*⊗_A C ≅ ∏_{σ≠1} C_σ. Here C_1 is the factor of the identity embedding, which carries the 1-dimensional Lie algebra; the other factors carry the dual part.

Tate's theorem (Hodge–Tate decomposition for p-divisible groups, 1966/67) then says the following. On each factor C_σ there is an A⊗C-linear isomorphism λ ↦ λx_σ that intertwines two Galois actions:
- the source action is the semilinear action twisted by χ_π (the '*' action);
- the target action is x ↦ g(x) for σ ≠ 1, and x ↦ τ(g)g(x) for σ = 1, where τ is the cyclotomic ('Tate') character.

Concretely, there exist x_σ ∈ C* with:
- g(x_σ) = σ(χ_π(g)) x_σ for σ ≠ 1;
- g(x_1) = τ(g)^{-1} χ_π(g) x_1.

NB, first point: each x_σ is a priori unique only up to a scalar. The note says the choice of one of them (say x_1) determines all the others canonically via Tate's theorem.

NB, second point (non-existence argument): there is no x'_1 ∈ C* with g(x'_1) = χ_π(g)x'_1 for g in inertia. If there were, put x = x'_1·∏_{σ≠1} x_σ. Then g(x) = N_{A/Q_ℓ}(χ_π(g)) x. On inertia, the norm of the Lubin–Tate character equals τ (local class field theory), so g(x) = τ(g)x on inertia. This contradicts Tate's theorem that C(1) has no nonzero invariants (C(1)^{I} = 0).

Purpose: to show that the Lubin–Tate character itself is not of Hodge–Tate weight 0, while its conjugates σ∘χ (σ ≠ 1) are. In other words, the Hodge–Tate weights are (1,0,…,0). This is the key input for Serre's openness / Lie-algebra results on Galois images.
errors: No real mathematical error. The τ^{-1} in the σ=1 condition is a sign/normalization convention and is consistent with the final step: N(χ)·τ^{-1} = 1 on inertia.
The identity N_{A/Q_ℓ}∘χ_π = τ holds on inertia only, possibly up to inverse depending on the normalization of the Artin map. Grothendieck correctly restricts to inertia.

The claim 'determines canonically all the others' is loosely stated. The x_σ for different σ are a priori independent choices up to scalars, unless further structure (e.g. the A-linear isomorphism) ties them together. Partly illegible.

ideas.what: Hodge–Tate decomposition of V_ℓ⊗C for a Lubin–Tate / CM formal group, split along the embeddings σ : A → C
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate decomposition for p-divisible groups; Hodge–Tate weights of Lubin–Tate characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (p-divisible groups, Driebergen 1966/67); Serre (Driebergen 1967; Abelian ℓ-adic representations, Ch. III)
ideas.where_published: Tate 'p-divisible groups'; Serre 'Sur les groupes de Galois attachés aux groupes p-divisibles' (1967)

ideas.what: Characters σ∘χ_π for σ≠1 are C-admissible of weight 0, while χ_π itself is not; proof by taking the product and using N∘χ = cyclotomic on inertia
ideas.modern_name: Lubin–Tate character has Hodge–Tate weights (1,0,…,0); Tate's theorem H^0(G_K, C(n)) = 0 for n≠0
ideas.where_published: Serre, Abelian ℓ-adic representations, Ch. III appendix; Driebergen proceedings

deep.surprise_reason: This is a private working-through of Tate's Hodge–Tate theorem applied to Lubin–Tate characters, essentially Serre's 1967 argument. It is of historical interest because it shows Grothendieck studying p-adic Hodge theory around the time of his 'Cristaux' work, but it contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '(τ étant la caractère[?] de Tate)' should read '(τ étant le caractère de Tate)', i.e. the cyclotomic character.
The NB line probably reads 'A priori, les x_σ sont déterminés par la condition à multiplication près par un élément de ... A*⊂K*⊂C*' rather than 'contre multiplication ... module'.
'pour g∈R (resp. = groupe d'inertie de R)' is more likely 'pour g ∈ I (I = inertie de π)' or similar; the condition is intended on inertia.
The norm subscript in the image looks like N_{A*/Q_ℓ}, meaning N_{A/Q_ℓ}.
The first line reads 'tenant compte des isom can. obtenus plus haut (de A⊗C-modules)'.
